title: HLS Runtime Lifecycle Boundary
problem: HLS session lifecycle, admission, readiness, segment waits, and cleanup are distributed across server playback composition, HLS app service, artifact service, transcode runner, and startup cleanup, which will make queueing, artifact I/O pressure, remote workers, and LL-HLS harder to add safely.
gates: git diff --check -- docs/workstreams/hls-runtime-lifecycle-boundary docs/architecture/PLAYBACK.md docs/architecture/LANES.md docs/architecture/WORKSTREAM_LINKS.md docs/workstreams/README.md

evidence.summary: Froze current HLS lifecycle invariants, cleanup ownership, readiness and one-shot segment wait semantics, test coverage map, and the decision to split artifact I/O pressure into a PAIP follow-on without changing Rust behavior.

continue_policy.notes: Continue with HRLB-020 only after planner review of the HRLB-010 invariant freeze. Keep HRLB-020 behavior-preserving and focused on lifecycle tests/coordinator boundaries. Do not implement PAIP artifact I/O pressure enforcement, resource admission unification, remote workers, LL-HLS/CMAF, Public/Admin DTOs, storage schema, or FFmpeg command planning until the planner splits or approves those scopes.
